## Global Context & Statement of Inquiry · 全球背景与探究陈述

**Global Context 全球背景: Fairness and Development 公平与发展**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

- **Core Inquiry 核心探究:** Power, authority and access to justice (权力、权威与司法正义).

## The Greek Polis: Geography & Autonomy · 群山阻隔与城邦自治

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

- **No hydraulic need 无大规模水利协作需求:** no giant floodplains, so no need for a centralized god-king.
- **The rise of the polis 城邦体制兴起:** each isolated valley became an independent, self-ruling {{< vocab "city-state" >}} — Athens, Sparta, Corinth.
- **Local patriotism 城邦自治忠诚:** loyalty belonged to one's own polis, not to a "Greek nation".

:::
::: {.column width="45%"}

**Bilingual anchor 双语锚点**

> **{{< vocab "city-state" text="Polis" >}}** 城邦 — a city plus the farmland around it, governing itself.

(|城市| + |国家| = one small, fiercely independent state)

**PACKET ACTION 手册操作 (page 3):**

Underline the **two** physical barriers, and write *ISOLATION* beside the sentence explaining why one king could not rule Greece.

:::
::::

---

## Athenian Direct Democracy on the Pnyx · 普尼克斯山丘上的直接民主

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

- **Direct voting 直接表决:** citizens voted on laws themselves in the {{< vocab "assembly" text="Ecclesia" >}} — they did not elect politicians to decide for them.
- **The Pnyx hill 普尼克斯山丘:** up to 6,000 adult male citizens gathered on the stone *bema* platform to debate.
- **Pericles' wage reform 津贴制:** public officials were paid a daily stipend, so poor citizens could afford to serve.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Primary source 一手史料 (431 BCE)**

> "Our constitution is called a {{< vocab "democracy" >}} because power is in the hands of the whole people."

— Pericles' Funeral Oration 伯里克利《国葬演说》

{{< timer 3 >}}

**Turn & Talk (60 s):** Pericles says "the whole people". Using the evidence on the next slide, is he right?

:::
::::

---

## The Democratic Paradox: Who Held Power? · 雅典民主的悖论

**Athens' population by group (estimated shares):**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

| Group 群体 | Share | Could vote? |
|---|---|---|
| Free adult male {{< vocab "citizen" text="citizens" >}} | ~12% | **Yes — the only group** |
| Women and children | ~35% | No |
| {{< vocab "metic" text="Metics" >}} (foreign residents) | ~18% | No — paid tax, rowed in the navy |
| Enslaved people | ~35% | No — {{< vocab "chattel slavery" text="chattel property" >}} |

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Active task 课堂活动 (page 5, Stage 2)**

Colour your pie chart, then finish this sentence:

> "Athenian democracy was an elite luxury subsidized by forced labour."

*雅典民主是建立在强迫劳动之上的精英特权。*

**Think about it:** free men could spend whole days debating philosophy in the Assembly only because enslaved workers mined silver at Laurion and farmed the estates.

:::
::::

---

## Sparta & Formative Checkpoint 1 · 斯巴达对比与第1课过关检测

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}

**The Spartan contrast 斯巴达对照**

- An {{< vocab "oligarchy" >}}: two hereditary kings, a council of elders, five overseers.
- Conquered neighbours were made state-owned serfs: {{< vocab "helot" text="helots" >}} — outnumbering citizens about **8 to 1**.
- Constant fear of revolt turned Sparta into a permanent army; boys entered barracks at age seven.
- Later, Alexander's campaigns spread Greek ideas eastward → {{< vocab "Hellenistic civilization" >}}.

:::
::: {.column width="55%"}

**Exit Ticket ET1 · 5 minutes, independent 独立作答**

1. **Factual 事实):** state **one** geographic reason why Greece developed separate {{< vocab "city-state" text="poleis" >}} rather than one unified river empire.
2. **Conceptual 概念):** name **two** groups shut out of voting in Athens, and {{< vocab "explain" >}} why that makes democracy a paradox.
3. **Application 迁移):** how did Alexander's conquests spread Hellenistic culture?

{{< timer 5 >}}

:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Collect ET1 before moving on. Most common misconception: helots are "slaves like Athens had". They were not private property — the Spartan state owned them and bound them to the land.
:::

## From Monarchy to the Roman Republic · 推翻王政：罗马共和国的诞生

**Lesson Objective 学习目标 (I can...):** explain how the Republic balanced power between {{< vocab "patrician" text="patricians" >}} and {{< vocab "plebeian" text="plebeians" >}}, and analyse how mass slavery made the Republic collapse into an {{< vocab "empire" >}}.

**Revolution of 509 BCE 公元前509年革命**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Overthrow of tyranny**

罗马人推翻伊特鲁里亚暴君，宣誓永不再立国王
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Res publica 公共事务**

a state whose supreme power belongs to citizens who elect representatives
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Two unequal classes**

{{< vocab "patrician" text="patricians" >}} 贵族 vs {{< vocab "plebeian" text="plebeians" >}} 平民
:::
::::

---

## The Architecture of Checks & Balances · 罗马共和国宪制三角

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}

| Branch | Who | Power |
|---|---|---|
| 1. **{{< vocab "consul" text="Consuls" >}}** 执政官 | Two elected magistrates, **1-year term** | Command the legions; each can veto the other |
| 2. **{{< vocab "senate" >}}** 元老院 | ~300 {{< vocab "patrician" text="patricians" >}}, **for life** | Treasury, foreign treaties |
| 3. **{{< vocab "tribune" text="Tribunes" >}}** 保民官 | Elected by plebeians | Forum veto check to protect commoners |

:::
::: {.column width="40%"}

**Bilingual anchor 双语锚点**

> **{{< vocab "veto" >}}** 否决权 — Latin for *"I forbid!"*

拉丁语原意：“我禁止！”

**PACKET TASK 手册操作 (page 9, Stage 1):**

Draw the arrows showing each branch checking the other two.

:::
::::

## Primary Source: The Twelve Tables (451 BCE) · 《十二铜表法》的双重面孔

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Table I — due process 第一表：诉讼正当程序**

> "If someone is summoned to court, he shall go."

- Laws carved on bronze ended secret {{< vocab "patrician" text="patrician" >}} court bias.
- Progress: public rules, burden of proof on the accuser.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Table VIII — injury and slaves 第八表：侵权与奴隶财产**

> Broken bone of a free man = 300 coins.
> Broken bone of a slave = 150 coins.

**Who received the 150 coins? The master.**
Slaves were {{< vocab "chattel slavery" text="property" >}}, not legal persons.

:::
::::

**Critical verdict 辩证结论:** real progress in written {{< vocab "due process" >}} for free citizens — and continued legal oppression for enslaved people.

---

## Conquest, Latifundia & the Fall of the Republic · 唯物史观四步因果链

**The four-step domino 四步历史骨牌:**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

1. **Conquest 军事扩张** — Rome beat Carthage in the Punic Wars; hundreds of thousands of war captives flooded Italy.
2. **{{< vocab "latifundia" >}} 大庄园** — {{< vocab "patrician" text="patricians" >}} bought farmland and ran it with unpaid enslaved workers.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

3. **Bankruptcy 小农破产** — free {{< vocab "plebeian" text="plebeian" >}} farmers could not compete with zero-cost slave labour, so they moved to Rome.
4. **Collapse 共和覆灭** — generals recruited desperate landless men into private armies → civil wars → Emperor Augustus in 27 BCE.

:::
::::

**Statistic 关键数据:** by 100 BCE about **33% (1 in 3)** of people in Roman Italy was enslaved. The Republic was eaten from the inside.

# Lesson 3 · Rivers vs. Seas {background-color="#003477"}

Cross-Civilization Synthesis & Summative Launch

## Master Comparative Matrix · 跨单元核心要素对比

**Continuity vs. Change 延续与变迁**

| Dimension | Unit 1: River valleys | Unit 2: Mediterranean | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Geography & power** | Floodplains → {{< vocab "theocracy" text="theocratic" >}} god-kings | Mountains & seas → assemblies, {{< vocab "republic" >}} | **Major change 重大变迁** |
| **2. Written law** | Hammurabi: {{< vocab "lex talionis" >}} scaled by rank | {{< vocab "Twelve Tables" >}}: public {{< vocab "due process" >}} for citizens | **Change** in procedure, **continuity** for slaves |
| **3. Labour regimes** | Peasant {{< vocab "corvee labor" >}} | Mass {{< vocab "chattel slavery" >}} (33% of Italy) | **Fundamental continuity 根本延续** |

{{< timer 8 >}}

## Summative Task Launch (GRASPS) · 终结性学术论文发布

**The Mingwan Academic Symposium Commission 明湾学校学术研讨会**

- **Role & goal 角色与目标:** as a junior comparative historian, write a **5-paragraph comparative essay (400–600 words)** judging whether classical systems were authentic progress.
- **Civilization pairing track 文明配对 (choose one 二选一):**
  - **Track A:** Mesopotamia (Hammurabi) vs. the Roman Republic ({{< vocab "Twelve Tables" >}} & {{< vocab "latifundia" >}})
  - **Track B:** Ancient Egypt (pharaoh {{< vocab "theocracy" >}}) vs. Classical Athens ({{< vocab "democracy" >}} & slavery)
- **HALT protocol 严禁 AI 生成:** supervised in-class drafting on Toddle, with a verified handwritten paper trail.
